name: Lisan al-Din ibn al-Khatib
bio: Muhammad ibn Abdallah ibn Sa'id al-Salmani, known as Lisan al-Din ibn al-Khatib, was an Andalusian vizier, historian and man of letters, born in 713 AH (1313 CE) to a family from Loja and raised in Granada. The Nasrid sultans of Granada, Abu al-Hajjaj Yusuf and then his son al-Ghani billah Muhammad, made him their vizier; he was called the holder of the two vizierates, of the pen and of the sword, and the man of two lives, because he wrote by night and governed by day, and he left some sixty books, among them al-Ihata, on the history of Granada. Al-Maqqari wrote his Nafh al-Tib in his name: its full title ends “and the memory of its vizier, Lisan al-Din ibn al-Khatib”. Sensing that rivals were working against him, he left al-Andalus secretly in 773 AH (1371–72 CE) for the Marinid sultan Abd al-Aziz and settled in Fez; after that sultan's death, Abu al-Abbas Ahmad took the throne with the help of al-Ghani billah, on conditions that included handing Ibn al-Khatib over, and arrested him; some jurists ruled that he should die, and he was strangled in prison in Fez in 776 AH (1374 CE) and buried in the cemetery of Bab al-Mahruq.
